segments.text: In this city, the average salary is fifty thousand.
segments.caption: In this city, the average salary is 50,000.

segments.text: Yet seven out of nine people earn less than that!
segments.caption: Yet 7 out of 9 people earn less than that!

segments.text: How can most people be below average?
segments.caption: How can most people be below average?

segments.text: The answer is skew.
segments.caption: The answer is skew.

segments.text: Skew means your data is lopsided.
segments.caption: Skew means your data is lopsided.

segments.text: Most values pile up on one side. A long tail stretches out the other way.
segments.caption: Most values pile up on one side. A long tail stretches out the other way.

segments.text: The tail's direction gives the skew its name.
segments.caption: The tail's direction gives the skew its name.

segments.text: There are three shapes.
segments.caption: There are three shapes.

segments.text: Symmetric, like heights: both sides match.
segments.caption: Symmetric, like heights: both sides match.

segments.text: Right-skewed, like salaries: a few huge values make a long tail to the right.
segments.caption: Right-skewed, like salaries: a few huge values make a long tail to the right.

segments.text: Left-skewed, like scores on an easy test: most score high, and a few trail off to the left.
segments.caption: Left-skewed, like scores on an easy test: most score high, and a few trail off to the left.

segments.text: Here's the key rule. The tail pulls the mean toward it.
segments.caption: Here's the key rule. The tail pulls the mean toward it.

segments.text: In right skew, the mean is dragged above the median, and the peak, the mode, sits lowest.
segments.caption: In right skew, the mean is dragged above the median, and the peak, the mode, sits lowest.

segments.text: In left skew, it flips. The mean falls below the median.
segments.caption: In left skew, it flips. The mean falls below the median.

segments.text: And when it's symmetric, they all meet in the middle.
segments.caption: And when it's symmetric, they all meet in the middle.

segments.text: To spot skew, compare the mean and the median.
segments.caption: To spot skew, compare the mean and the median.

segments.text: Mean above the median? Right skew. Below it? Left skew.
segments.caption: Mean above the median? Right skew. Below it? Left skew.

segments.text: Or look at a box plot: the longer whisker points to the tail.
segments.caption: Or look at a box plot: the longer whisker points to the tail.

segments.text: Why does it matter? In skewed data, the mean misleads.
segments.caption: Why does it matter? In skewed data, the mean misleads.

segments.text: That city's typical salary is the median: thirty thousand, not fifty.
segments.caption: That city's typical salary is the median: 30,000, not 50.

segments.text: So report the median and IQR, or log-transform the data to balance it.
segments.caption: So report the median and IQR, or log-transform the data to balance it.

segments.text: Here's the complete picture.
segments.caption: Here's the complete picture.

segments.text: Symmetric: the mean equals the median.
segments.caption: Symmetric: the mean equals the median.

segments.text: Right skew: the mean is above the median, tail to the right.
segments.caption: Right skew: the mean is above the median, tail to the right.

segments.text: Left skew: the mean is below the median, tail to the left.
segments.caption: Left skew: the mean is below the median, tail to the left.

segments.text: Quick quiz!
segments.caption: Quick quiz!

segments.text: Most people recharge their phone for two hundred rupees, but a few pay two thousand.
segments.caption: Most people recharge their phone for 200 rupees, but a few pay 2,000.

segments.text: Which way is it skewed?
segments.caption: Which way is it skewed?

segments.text: Right-skewed!
segments.caption: Right-skewed!

segments.text: The few big recharges make a long tail to the right, and pull the mean above the median.
segments.caption: The few big recharges make a long tail to the right, and pull the mean above the median.
